(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from

(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the

`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# MCP Server Instructions

Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. D1 through D61 are all fixed or, in D35's case, deliberately
downgraded to a stale reading with a way to refresh it. §1.1 records what each was and why the
chosen fix was the right one — including the three that were answered by
*removing* something rather than making it work: D8's write-only CRUD flags,
D21's unreachable clamp and D36's never-filled cache.

The five that stayed open longest — D4, D8, D9, D10 and D11 — were parked not
because they were hard but because each altered something the user already saw,
so they needed a deliberate call rather than a drive-by fix. All five were then
decided together and fixed in one pass; see [§1.2](#12-the-five-parked-defects).

### 1.1 Fixed

====
**D152 — DEVDESK-470: the Diagnostics form gets a Trace Path sub-level that reuses the Path tab's engine. Decided (user, 2026-11-15): (1) The sub-level of the Diagnostics form runs on the single `m.pathModel` instance, not a second one. A second instance would accept `pathResolvedMsg`, `pathHopMsg` and `pathDoneMsg` (which carry only the generation, with counters at 0) in both places. Cost, accepted: the target field of the Path tab receives the form's target, as `H` does, and any text being typed there is overwritten, until P2-02 (removal of the Path tab). (2) No `ctrl+o` and no relaunch inside the sub-level: to relaunch, `esc` then activate Trace Path again. (3) `enter` on a text field always runs Run Diagnostics; a trace starts only from its button. (4) When Port or DNS Server is filled in, the trace runs on the target alone, with an Info notice in the footer. (5) The refusal of Run Diagnostics is unchanged (a timed error, no underline). Only Trace Path applies Rule 140 (invalid field underlined, error also in the footer). (6) The Trace Path button is greyed, with its reason in the footer permanently, when the platform does not support the trace (DEVDESK-334). Reference: D150 point 5 (the net view redesign, option P2, comes after DEVDESK-335). Why: one engine, one generation counter, so the two views cannot answer for each other. No ADR: local and reversible. **Plane:** DEVDESK-470, decided by the maintainer on 2026-11-15. Shipped with DEVDESK-470. Sources: `internal/ui/netdiag/trace_form.go`, `trace_level.go`, `.claude/plans/net-view-ux-audit.md`, D150, D151.**
**D144 — DEVDESK-328 (S-03b; point 3 superseded in part by D150): the path trace has a fifth tab, Path, in the network view. Decided: (1) Path is the fifth tab, last. (2) Streaming is a callback of the engine, `nettrace.TraceEach(ctx, target, opts, onHop)`, not a field of `Options`, which stays comparable (`Trace` calls it with nil). The engine may report a hop above the terminal one, so the UI reconciles with `Result.Hops` at done. (3) The target field takes `host` or `host:port`: the port is validated and shown in the header, but has no effect on the probes, which stay UDP to port 33435 (option A). *Superseded in part by D150: a port is now refused, not shown.* (4) `H` (`keymap.Diagnose`) on the Local route row of Diagnostics opens Path prefilled with the host only, and never launches; `enter` launches, `esc` cancels. (5) Error labels are fixed texts; the system error text goes to the log only. The body is always the hop table; the target sits in the bar slot. Hypotheses (prudent defaults, not validated): 30 hops, 3 s per probe and 30 s overall (engine defaults); the first IPv4 address when a name resolves to several; `enter` greyed outside supported Linux and refused with a Warn. Why: the plan `.claude/plans/devdesk-328-path-tab-plan.md` (main checkout) keeps `Options` comparable and gives the view a single streamed source; `H` prefills without sending, since nothing leaves before an explicit `enter`. No ADR: local and reversible. **Plane:** DEVDESK-328 (S-03b), dated 2026-11-14. Sources: the plan above, D143, worktree `.worktrees/feat/devdesk-328-path-tab` (uncommitted when this entry was written).**

lines: **D145 — DEVDESK-329 (S-04): the Path column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway. Decided: (1) The route (interface, source address, gateway) is read by `netcheck.Env.Route` in the trace producer, for the traced address, and carried by `pathResolvedMsg`. The `route` stage is not re-run and its facts (display strings) are not parsed. Rejected: re-running the stage and parsing its facts (parses display text); the local address of the trace socket, `getsockname` in `nettrace` (no interface name, no gateway, and it widens `nettrace` for a UI concern); reusing the Diagnostics result on the `H` path (stale, exists only on that path, and Diagnostics may route several addresses where the trace uses the first). No new message: the result rides on `pathResolvedMsg`, so the channel capacity is unchanged. go-netroute asks the kernel the question `ip route get` asks (policy rules applied), and the trace socket is unmarked and unbound, so the interface row and the probes agree; under a full-tunnel VPN the row names the tunnel. (2) One row type, `pathStep`, four kinds (source, interface, gateway, hop); `pathSteps` is the only place that orders the column. (3) The source row is always `this machine`, never `os.Hostname()`: under WSL2 the distro host name defaults to the Windows computer name and would label the source as another machine. Its address is on the interface row. (4) Column 2 is renamed `Answer` → `Step`: `source`, `interface` and `gateway` are not answers. (5) A route lookup error is not fatal: the rows read `undetermined`, the trace still runs, and the raw error goes to the log only (`ERROR [netdiag/path] route …`). (6) Nothing is shown before the route is known (empty table, `Resolving …`); the source row appears with the first row. (7) The footer counter counts hop rows only. (8) A trace error clears every row, as DEVDESK-328 did; reading failures is S-09. Hypotheses (prudent defaults, not validated): local rows have an empty Hop and RTT, not `-` (`-` means no answer); the gateway row stays when it repeats hop 1; no gateway reads `directly connected`; no interface name reads `unnamed (address)`. Why: the plan `.claude/plans/devdesk-329-path-column-plan.md` (worktree `.worktrees/feat/devdesk-329-path-column`, uncommitted when this entry was written); acceptance criteria 1 to 5 of Plane DEVDESK-329. No ADR: local, reversible, one view, no public API. **Plane:** DEVDESK-329 (S-04), dated 2026-11-14. Sources: the plan above, D144, D-a to D-d of the plan.**

The engine may report a hop above the terminal one, so the UI reconciles with `Result.Hops` at done. (3) The target field takes `host` or `host:port`: the port is validated and shown in the header, but has no effect on the probes, which stay UDP to port 33435 (option A). *Superseded in part by D150: a port is now refused, not shown.* (4) `H` (`keymap.Diagnose`) on the Local route row of Diagnostics opens Path prefilled with the host only, and never launches; `enter` launches, `esc` cancels. (5) Error labels are fixed texts; the system error text goes to the log only. The body is always the hop table; the target sits in the bar slot. **D143 — DEVDESK-327 (S-03a): the native path trace is UDP + `IP_RECVERR`, one socket per TTL, Linux only, in two phases, with simultaneous sends; a router's Unreachable ends the trace, and non-unicast targets are refused. `internal/nettrace` opens one connected UDP socket per TTL (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`) and reads the ICMP answer from the error queue: no raw socket, no privilege, no external binary, no container. Phase 1 opens all N sockets, phase 2 probes in parallel, so "unsupported" or "no route" is known before anything is sent. The N probes leave together, not spread out. A Destination Unreachable from a router (`HopUnreachable`) ends the trace like a reached target, with `OutcomeUnreachable`. `0.0.0.0`, multicast and `255.255.255.255` get `ErrNotUnicast`; an IPv6 target gets `ErrNotIPv4` (IPv4 only, decided before S-01). Other platforms return `ErrUnsupported`. Why: spikes S-01 (native Linux, DEVDESK-325) and S-02 (WSL2 NAT and mirrored, DEVDESK-326) measured it unprivileged (uid 1000, no capability), no leak on cancellation, about 3 s for 30 TTLs; and the container trace of §3.47 answered for the wrong machine. Arbitrations by the user, 2026-11-14: simultaneous sends (S-01 suggested spreading them out, because the number of answering hops varies, 6 to 10, which was hypothesized, not verified, to come from ICMP rate limiting; a prober timing defect is not ruled out; not retained), a router's Unreachable as terminal, non-unicast targets refused. Known and accepted: that variability (observed on WSL2 NAT and native Linux, cause unverified), a multi-homed target answering from another address is not recognized as reached, and a duration of about `ProbeTimeout` once a hop before the target is silent. `golang.org/x/sys` becomes a direct dependency (Rule 303). `Supported()` is not wired to the UI yet and `traceroute_max_hops` stays removed. No ADR: local and reversible.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-327 (S-03a), documentation task DEVDESK-418, dated 2026-11-14. Sources: `docs/product/network-map/{feasibility,spike-linux,spike-wsl}.md`, `docs/architecture/network.md` (The path trace), D57 (no `--network host` left), worktree `.worktrees/feat/devdesk-327-nettrace` (uncommitted when this entry was written).

Sources: the plan above, D143, worktree `.worktrees/feat/devdesk-328-path-tab` (uncommitted when this entry was written).**

+**D144 — DEVDESK-328 (S-03b; point 3 superseded in part by D150): the path trace has a fifth tab, Path, in the network view. Decided: (1) Path is the fifth tab, last. *Superseded by D153 point 1: the Path tab is removed.* (2) Streaming is a callback of the engine, `nettrace.TraceEach(ctx, target, opts, onHop)`, not a field of `Options`, which stays comparable (`Trace` calls it with nil). The engine may report a hop above the terminal one, so the UI reconciles with `Result.Hops` at done. (3) The target field takes `host` or `host:port`: the port is validated and shown in the header, but has no effect on the probes, which stay UDP to port 33435 (option A). *Superseded in part by D150: a port is now refused, not shown.* (4) `H` (`keymap.Diagnose`) on the Local route row of Diagnostics opens Path prefilled with the host only, and never launches; `enter` launches, `esc` cancels. *Its Path tab is replaced by the trace level (D153 point 2); the rest stands.* (5) Error labels are fixed texts; the system error text goes to the log only. The body is always the hop table; the target sits in the bar slot. Hypotheses (prudent defaults, not validated): 30 hops, 3 s per probe and 30 s overall (engine defaults); the first IPv4 address when a name resolves to several; `enter` greyed outside supported Linux and refused with a Warn. Why: the plan `.claude/plans/devdesk-328-path-tab-plan.md` (main checkout) keeps `Options` comparable and gives the view a single streamed source; `H` prefills without sending, since nothing leaves before an explicit `enter`. No ADR: local and reversible. **Plane:** DEVDESK-328 (S-03b), dated 2026-11-14. Sources: the plan above, D143, worktree `.worktrees/feat/devdesk-328-path-tab` (uncommitted when this entry was written).**

**D143 — DEVDESK-327 (S-03a): the native path trace is UDP + `IP_RECVERR`, one socket per TTL, Linux only, in two phases, with simultaneous sends; a router's Unreachable ends the trace, and non-unicast targets are refused. `internal/nettrace` opens one connected UDP socket per TTL (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`) and reads the ICMP answer from the error queue: no raw socket, no privilege, no external binary, no container. Phase 1 opens all N sockets, phase 2 probes in parallel, so "unsupported" or "no route" is known before anything is sent. The N probes leave together, not spread out. A Destination Unreachable from a router (`HopUnreachable`) ends the trace like a reached target, with `OutcomeUnreachable`. `0.0.0.0`, multicast and `255.255.255.255` get `ErrNotUnicast`; an IPv6 target gets `ErrNotIPv4` (IPv4 only, decided before S-01). Other platforms return `ErrUnsupported`. Why: spikes S-01 (native Linux, DEVDESK-325) and S-02 (WSL2 NAT and mirrored, DEVDESK-326) measured it unprivileged (uid 1000, no capability), no leak on cancellation, about 3 s for 30 TTLs; and the container trace of §3.47 answered for the wrong machine. Arbitrations by the user, 2026-11-14: simultaneous sends (S-01 suggested spreading them out, because the number of answering hops varies, 6 to 10, which was hypothesized, not verified, to come from ICMP rate limiting; a prober timing defect is not ruled out; not retained), a router's Unreachable as terminal, non-unicast targets refused. Known and accepted: that variability (observed on WSL2 NAT and native Linux, cause unverified), a multi-homed target answering from another address is not recognized as reached, and a duration of about `ProbeTimeout` once a hop before the target is silent. `golang.org/x/sys` becomes a direct dependency (Rule 303). `Supported()` is not wired to the UI yet and `traceroute_max_hops` stays removed. No ADR: local and reversible.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-327 (S-03a), documentation task DEVDESK-418, dated 2026-11-14. Sources: `docs/product/network-map/{feasibility,spike-linux,spike-wsl}.md`, `docs/architecture/network.md` (The path trace), D57 (no `--network host` left), worktree `.worktrees/feat/devdesk-327-nettrace` (uncommitted when this entry was written).

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, native Linux and WSL2 only: on macOS, Windows and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`), the tab progress bar (OSC 9;4, `terminalProgress`), the window title (`windowTitle`, restored by `internal/termtitle`), the terminal hand-off to child processes (the exec wrapper `internal/ui/teaexec`, use it instead of `tea.ExecProcess`, D121) and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci` (typed `StatusError`, `...Context` variants), `internal/imagesearch` and the registry browser's image search level, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface`, `internal/nettrace` (the path trace: unprivileged UDP + `IP_RECVERR`, Linux only) |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage`, `internal/ui/datatable`, and the activity indicator column (`internal/ui/indicator`, `datatable.IndicatorColumn`, the row sentences `components.DescribeRow`) |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator

- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata

`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `golang.org/x/sys` - direct (Rule 303): the socket calls of `internal/nettrace` (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`, `recvmsg` on the error queue)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, native Linux and WSL2 only: on macOS, Windows and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |

| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

lines: ### 1.1 Fixed

-**D153 — DEVDESK-471 (P2-02): the Path tab is removed; the path trace survives only as the trace level of Diagnostics. Decided (user, 2026-11-15): (1) The network view has four tabs: Diagnostics, Ports, Interfaces, Forward. *Supersedes point 1 of D144 (Path as the fifth tab).* (2) `H` on the Local route row opens the trace level on the results' target, in the ready state, and never starts a trace. `enter` starts it. D144 point 4 stands, its "Path tab" now read as this trace level. (3) Inside the trace level, `enter` starts a trace and also restarts it ("Trace again") once a trace has ended or been cancelled. `ctrl+o` opens "Trace from", a declared keymap exception (`netdiag/trace`, replacing `netdiag/path`). `esc` cancels a running trace, then returns to the origin screen (form or results) with its state. *Supersedes point 2 of D152 (no `ctrl+o` and no relaunch in the sub-level).* (4) `PathModel` has no target field: the target comes from the form, entered once. *Ends the cost accepted in point 1 of D152.* (5) `H` and Trace Path are greyed, with their reason, on a platform that cannot trace and on a target the trace refuses (for example an IPv6 literal). (6) Changing the source returns to the ready state and starts nothing. (7) `esc` on the prefilled form opened from Status is unchanged: it does nothing, as today (AC6, option b). Hypotheses: H1 to H7 of the plan, prudent defaults, not validated. Out of scope, to track in a dedicated Plane ticket (not yet created): the cursor blink of the Diagnostics form is lost after `restoreFormFocus` and `moveFocus`, because the `Cmd` returned by `Focus()` is dropped; it predates this change for `moveFocus`. Why: one trace surface, no duplicated target field, and the trace stays opt-in (D144 point 4). No ADR: local and reversible by a revert. **Plane:** DEVDESK-471. Sources: `.claude/plans/devdesk-471-remove-path-tab-plan.md`, D144, D150 point 5, D152, the audit `.claude/plans/net-view-ux-audit.md` (option P2).**

+**D153 — DEVDESK-471 (P2-02): the Path tab is removed; the path trace survives only as the trace level of Diagnostics. Decided (user, 2026-11-15): (1) The network view has four tabs: Diagnostics, Ports, Interfaces, Forward. *Supersedes point 1 of D144 (Path as the fifth tab).* (2) `H` on the Local route row opens the trace level on the results' target, in the ready state, and never starts a trace. `enter` starts it. D144 point 4 stands, its "Path tab" now read as this trace level. (3) Inside the trace level, `enter` starts a trace and also restarts it ("Trace again") once a trace has ended or been cancelled. `ctrl+o` opens "Trace from", a declared keymap exception (`netdiag/trace`, replacing `netdiag/path`). `esc` cancels a running trace, then returns to the origin screen (form or results) with its state. *Supersedes point 2 of D152 (no `ctrl+o` and no relaunch in the sub-level).* (4) `PathModel` has no target field: the target comes from the form, entered once. *Ends the cost accepted in point 1 of D152.* (5) `H` and Trace Path are greyed, with their reason, on a platform that cannot trace and on a target the trace refuses (for example an IPv6 literal). (6) Changing the source returns to the ready state and starts nothing. (7) `esc` on the prefilled form opened from Status is unchanged: it does nothing, as today (AC6, option b). Hypotheses: H1 to H7 of the plan, prudent defaults, not validated. Out of scope, tracked in Plane as DEVDESK-485: the cursor blink of the Diagnostics form is lost after `restoreFormFocus` and `moveFocus`, because the `Cmd` returned by `Focus()` is dropped; it predates this change for `moveFocus`. Why: one trace surface, no duplicated target field, and the trace stays opt-in (D144 point 4). No ADR: local and reversible by a revert. **Plane:** DEVDESK-471. Sources: `.claude/plans/devdesk-471-remove-path-tab-plan.md`, D144, D150 point 5, D152, the audit `.claude/plans/net-view-ux-audit.md` (option P2).**

**D152 — DEVDESK-470: the Diagnostics form gets a Trace Path sub-level that reuses the Path tab's engine. Decided (user, 2026-11-15): (1) The sub-level of the Diagnostics form runs on the single `m.pathModel` instance, not a second one. A second instance would accept `pathResolvedMsg`, `pathHopMsg` and `pathDoneMsg` (which carry only the generation, with counters at 0) in both places. Cost, accepted: the target field of the Path tab receives the form's target, as `H` does, and any text being typed there is overwritten, until P2-02 (removal of the Path tab). *Ended by D153 point 4.* (2) No `ctrl+o` and no relaunch inside the sub-level: to relaunch, `esc` then activate Trace Path again. *Superseded by D153 point 3: `ctrl+o` and `enter` (relaunch) work inside the trace level.* (3) `enter` on a text field always runs Run Diagnostics; a trace starts only from its button. (4) When Port or DNS Server is filled in, the trace runs on the target alone, with an Info notice in the footer. (5) The refusal of Run Diagnostics is unchanged (a timed error, no underline). Only Trace Path applies Rule 140 (invalid field underlined, error also in the footer). (6) The Trace Path button is greyed, with its reason in the footer permanently, when the platform does not support the trace (DEVDESK-334). Reference: D150 point 5 (the net view redesign, option P2, comes after DEVDESK-335). Why: one engine, one generation counter, so the two views cannot answer for each other. No ADR: local and reversible. **Plane:** DEVDESK-470, decided by the maintainer on 2026-11-15. Shipped with DEVDESK-470. Sources: `internal/ui/netdiag/trace_form.go`, `trace_level.go`, `.claude/plans/net-view-ux-audit.md`, D150, D151.**
